newsitem.title: Netherlands: FOCUS-Oce ups payout, promises higher profit.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Oce ups payout, promises higher profit.

text.p: Printer and copier maker Oce-van der Grinten NV said on Monday net profits jumped 57 percent in 1995/96 and it promised further earnings growth for the current year.
The company said net profit for the year ended November 30, 1996 mushroomed to 169.5 million guilders ($89.2 million) from 108.3 million, due in part to a major acquisition in Germany.
Full-year sales rose 42 percent to 4.17 billion guilders, with SNI Printing, acquired from Germany's Siemens AG last April, accounting for just under half the increase.
Chairman Harry Pennings indicated at a news conference that he expected growth in net profit in the current year to outstrip the expected sales growth of at least 19.9 percent.

Helped by the full-year consolidation of SNI and the recent takeover of Messerli of Switzerland, sales in 1996/97 were expected to grow to at least 5.0 billion guilders from the previous year's 4.17 billion, Pennings said.
"It is expected that profit growth will outstrip sales growth in percentage terms (in 1996/97)," he added.
The company said it planned to raise its dividend to 3.00 guilders per share from 2.50 and that new product launches would contribute to a further improvement in earnings in 1996/97.
"Favourable business developments in 1996 and the positive expectations for 1997 are the most important reasons...to propose this (dividend increase)," Pennings said.

SNI Printing -- bought for 900 million guilders -- posted sales of 731 million guilders from April to the end of Oce's 1995/96 financial year. Oce said SNI Printing had also made an important contribution to group profits.
"Looking at the turnover figures, it (SNI Printing) has been performing very satisfactorily," board member Han Meertens said.

SNI sales had risen by an estimated 10 percent annually since the acquisition, Meertens added, noting that when Oce acquired SNI last year, the unit had annual sales totalling around one billion guilders.

Pennings said the takeover had reaped instant benefits. "The partnership bore fruit in the market almost immediately. Several important orders were booked in which Oce and SNI Printing were part of the same deal," he said.
The merger of SNI with Oce's existing printer activities had also reduced Oce's risk profile, Pennings added.
Oce said sales of equipment to the engineering systems market rose by 15 percent to 1.37 billion guilders, mainly because of strong sales of high volume digital copiers.
It said digital machines now represented more than 70 percent of its sales in the engineering systems market.
"Oce has been able to further bolster its leading position in this market which grows structurally by some two to four percent a year," Pennings said.
Sales in the office systems market, including printers sold under Oce's own name, rose 19 percent to 2.08 billion guilders.
"This growth clearly outstripped overall market growth... estimated at one or two percent a year worldwide," Pennings said.
SNI Printing booked strong sales for its Pagestream printers which can print at speeds of 700 pages per minute, Oce said.
"On the basis of its own strengths, Oce has expanded in all markets. The acquisition of SNI Printing has added a further important dimension to that expansion," the company said.
Oce said it would ask shareholders to approve a change in its official name to Oce NV from the more cumbersome Oce-van der Grinten NV.

On the Amsterdam Stock Exchange, Oce shares opened one guilder higher at 242.00 guilders on the results, touching a high of 242.50 guilders before dipping to 239.50 despite a sharply firmer midafternoon bourse. ($ = 1.899 Dutch Guilders)
